From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Mohamed Khan <mohamed.k@hedgesolutions.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Evaluation kickoff: scheduling & data access checklist

Hi Sara / Mohamed —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we can lock in the technical deep dive + formal evaluation kickoff:

Key outcomes from discovery:
- Primary use case: automated medical coding suggestions for post-visit notes (paraphrase + code mapping).
- Volume profile: ~150–300 notes/day, peak bursts up to 1,000/day.
- Success criteria: 85% top-1 coding accuracy on holdout set, <350ms median inference latency for single-note flow, and no PHI leakage in logs.

Proposed next steps (want to get these on calendar this week):
1) Technical deep dive (45–60m) — solution architecture, data access, model variants, and SE Q&A.
2) Evaluation kickoff (30–45m) — confirm success criteria, hand off prompt/eval set, align on timeline & MMP.

I have the following calendar windows available (PT):
- Thu 19 Nov — 10:00–11:00 or 15:00–16:00 PT
- Fri 20 Nov — 09:00–10:00 or 13:00–14:00 PT

Can you confirm which of these works for you? If none, send 2–3 preferred times and we’ll accommodate.

Practical asks ahead of the kickoff:
- Please review the attached Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx and Eval_Data_Access_Checklist.pdf — these list the minimal artifacts we’ll need (sample notes, schema, and preferred S3 share or secure upload).
- If your security/compliance team needs a heads-up, we can loop in Marcus (CC’d) to cover deployment and KMS options.

I’ll loop in Ben (SE) for the deep dive once we confirm a time.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0123

Thanks for the concise recap. 10:00–11:00 PT on Thu 19 Nov works for Mohamed and me for the technical deep dive. We’d prefer to combine the technical deep dive and the evaluation kickoff into a single 75-minute block if possible — saves scheduling for our team.

A couple quick clarifying points before we meet:
- About success criteria — the 85% top-1 coding accuracy is our target; can you confirm whether Redwood will evaluate against our internal gold set or if we should prepare a separate holdout/export?

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation kickoff: scheduling & data access checklist

Thanks Sara — combining the sessions into a single 75-minute block is fine. I’ve penciled Thu 19 Nov, 10:00–11:15 PT. I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Answers to your questions:
- Evaluation gold set: we prefer you provide a single holdout export (your internal gold set) that we don’t train on. That makes the evaluation results directly comparable to your benchmarks. If you’d rather we run checks against a redacted copy first, we can do that as a pre-check.
- Data ingress: IP whitelist + temporary S3 IAM role is perfect for the initial ingest. On the checklist we also ask for a sample of 50–100 de-identified notes and the schema mapping (fields for note text, encounter id, timestamps, existing codes).

What we’ll cover in the 75-minute session (proposed agenda):
- 0–10m: Introductions & goals (Tessa)
- 10–35m: Architecture and deployment options (Marcus) — hosted vs dedicated, KMS and audit logs
- 35–65m: SE deep dive (Ben) — prompt engineering, batching expectations, KV/prefix caching behavior, model variant suggestions (redwood-1.3-quant and redwood-1.4-fp16)
- 65–75m: Evaluation plan & immediate next steps — confirm success criteria, hand off prompt set (sample prompts requested below), timeline and MMP review

Immediate asks from our side (if you can prepare before the call, it will help speed the kickoff):
- Share the 50–100 sample de-identified notes (S3 link) + schema doc.
- Provide 10–15 representative prompts / sample inputs you want to test (e.g., raw note -> suggested codes; note -> summary + code).
- Confirm who on your team will own the S3 IAM role creation so Marcus can coordinate the IP whitelist and KMS options.

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx and Eval_Data_Access_Checklist.pdf (same as earlier).

If that agenda looks good, please reply "confirm" and I’ll send the calendar invite with Ben/Marcus included.

Onward —
Tessa
